source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 9–10, Theorem 6 and the paragraph immediately after its displayed lower bound
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 6 defines P_NP by i.i.d. sampling, a continuous bounded density on compact support, a rectifiable support boundary, Hölder regression smoothness, and continuous bounded variance; it then gives the n^{-1/4} distance-only lower bound. Assumption 2(iv), the uniform Gram-eigenvalue condition, is not among those theorem conditions. The following discussion says the log^{1/4} factor in the upper rate is conjectured unimprovable because Theorem 6 uses pointwise minimax arguments.

Remove ass:boundary-length-envelope from def:smooth-class, retaining it only for the rectifiable class, and state the length bounds as a derived consequence of the smooth chart envelopes.

Add a standalone primitive lemma establishing exactly which local-mass and density hypotheses imply the uniform Gram lower bound needed for the local-polynomial upper argument, including its dependence on p and K.
